title: Casper and the Static
premise: Oscar Marchetti, navigator of the freighter Casper, discovers that the mysterious beacon he maintains is broadcasting a forged ceasefire signal — a lie invented by the ship's dead captain to keep two hostile fleets from annihilating each other over a disputed colony. When a manifest lists a name belonging to a ship that never flew, Oscar realizes someone is decoding the forgery, and both fleets are converging on the truth. To keep the peace alive, he must rally the ship's misfit crew and the colony's outcasts into an unlikely family, forging a real accord before the static collapses. In the end, Oscar sacrifices his own record and freedom, broadcasting himself as the beacon's living author so the lie becomes a truth both fleets can accept.
about_author: Lena Brightwater is a former radio astronomer who traded observatory nights for writing mornings, drawn to stories about signals, silence, and the people who listen between them. She lives near a decommissioned tracking station and insists her best ideas arrive as interference.

chapters.title: The Beacon Nobody Ordered
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. During a routine maintenance shift, Oscar tends the ancient beacon in the hold, talking to it like a friend while the backups of dead crew sleep beside it. He notices its power draw has changed — someone or something is feeding it extra energy. Emotional beat: lonely devotion shadowed by first unease.

chapters.title: A Name That Never Flew
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Auditing old manifests to trace the beacon's origin, Oscar finds a ship listed that was never built, crewed by a name he's never heard: Vess Andrade. The Casper's quartermaster, Juno, warns him to stop digging. Emotional beat: curiosity curdling into dread as the paperwork refuses to add up.

chapters.title: Static in the Hold
chapters.summary: Juno's POV. Juno reveals fragments of the truth: the beacon broadcasts a forged ceasefire authored by Captain Reyes before her death, holding two fleets apart for six years. The extra energy means someone off-ship is answering the signal. Emotional beat: reluctant confession, the weight of inherited secrets.

chapters.title: Vess
chapters.summary: Vess Andrade's POV, transmitted via the beacon itself. A decoder aboard the warship Kestrel has been listening for years; she is the archivist assigned to prove the ceasefire false. She contacts Oscar not to destroy him but because she suspects the forgery saved her own homeworld. Emotional beat: wary connection across impossible distance.

chapters.title: Two Fleets, One Lie
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. The Casper's captain-elect, Brannoc, wants to sell the secret to the highest bidder; the crew splits. Oscar argues the lie is the only justice either fleet has known. Emotional beat: found family fracturing under the temptation of profit and fear.

chapters.title: The Kestrel Arrives
chapters.summary: Vess's POV. Vess defects, boarding the Casper with proof that her fleet's admiralty plans to expose the forgery and strike the colony within weeks. Juno takes her in; Brannoc locks down the hold. Emotional beat: a stranger becoming kin faster than trust can justify.

chapters.title: What the Backups Remember
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Oscar wakes Captain Reyes's backup briefly; she confirms she forged the ceasefire after witnessing a massacre both fleets blamed on each other. Her guilt and clarity gut him. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into resolve — the lie must become true.

chapters.title: Brannoc's Bargain
chapters.summary: Brannoc's POV. Cornered by his own crew, Brannoc transmits the forgery's coordinates to both fleets anyway, gambling that chaos will make him indispensable. The Casper's family turns on him, and Oscar must choose between mutiny and mercy. Emotional bet: power corrupting a good man too tired to resist it.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV, climax. With both fleets inbound, Oscar merges the beacon with his own neural implant and broadcasts the whole truth — the massacre, the forgery, Reyes's sacrifice — in his own voice, taking authorship of the lie. Fleets halt at the edge of weapons range. Emotional beat: self-sacrifice as the only honest signature.

chapters.title: Signal, Answered
chapters.summary: Vess's POV, resolution. Weeks later, the colony hosts the first joint tribunal held outside any fleet's law; Oscar, stripped of rank but not of crew, stands as witness. Vess archives the truth permanently. The beacon still hums — no longer a lie, just a lighthouse. Emotional beat: quiet belonging, justice made by hand.
